H5329: properly, to glitter from afar, i.e. to be eminent (as a superintendent, especially of the Temple services and its music); to be permanent
H4210: properly, instrumental music; by implication, a poem set to notes
H1732: David, the youngest son of Jesse
H8085: to hear intelligently (often with implication of attention, obedience, etc.; causatively, to tell, etc.)
H430: gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative
H7879: a contemplation; by implication, an utterance
H6343: a (sudden) alarm (properly, the object feared, by implication, the feeling)
H5341: to guard, in a good sense (to protect, maintain, obey, etc.) or a bad one (to conceal, etc.)
H2416: alive; hence, raw (flesh); fresh (plant, water, year), strong; also (as noun, especially in the feminine singular and masculine plural) life (or living thing), whether literally or figuratively
H5641: to hide (by covering), literally or figuratively
H5475: a session, i.e. company of persons (in close deliberation); by implication, intimacy, consultation, a secret
H7489: properly, to spoil (literally, by breaking to pieces); figuratively, to make (or be) good fornothing, i.e. bad (physically, socially or morally)
H6466: to do or make (systematically and habitually), especially to practise
H205: strictly nothingness; also trouble. vanity, wickedness; specifically an idol
H834: who, which, what, that; also (as an adverb and a conjunction) when, where, how, because, in order that, etc.
H8150: to point (transitive or intransitive); intensively, to pierce; figuratively, to inculcate
H2719: drought; also a cutting instrument (from its destructive effect), as a knife, sword, or other sharp implement
H3956: the tongue (of man or animals), used literally (as the instrument of licking, eating, or speech), and figuratively (speech, an ingot, a fork of flame, a cove of water)
H1869: to tread; by implication, to walk; also to string abow (by treading on it in bending)
H2671: properly, a piercer, i.e. an arrow; by implication, a wound; figuratively, (of God) thunderbolt; the shaft of aspear
H1697: a word; by implication, a matter (as spoken of) or thing; adverbially, a cause
H4751: bitter (literally or figuratively); also (as noun) bitterness, or (adverbially) bitterly
H3384: properly, to flow as water (i.e. to rain); transitively, to lay or throw (especially an arrow, i.e. to shoot); figuratively, to point out (as if by aiming the finger), to teach
H4565: properly, a concealer, i.e. a covert
H8535: complete; usually (morally) pious; specifically, gentle, dear
H3808: not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles
H3372: to fear; morally, to revere; caus. to frighten
H2388: to fasten upon; hence, to seize, be strong (figuratively, courageous, causatively strengthen, cure, help, repair, fortify), obstinate; to bind, restrain, conquer
H7451: bad or (as noun) evil (natural or moral)
H5608: properly, to score with a mark as a tally or record, i.e. (by implication) to inscribe, and also to enumerate; intensively, to recount, i.e. celebrate
H4170: a noose (for catching animals) (literally or figuratively); by implication, a hook (for the nose)
H4310: who? (occasionally, by a peculiar idiom, of things); also (indefinitely) whoever; often used in oblique construction with prefix or suffix
H7200: to see, literally or figuratively (in numerous applications, direct and implied, transitive, intransitive and causative)
H2664: to seek; causatively, to conceal oneself (i.e. let be sought), or mask
H8552: to complete, in a good or a bad sense, literal, or figurative, transitive or intransitive
H7130: properly, the nearest part, i.e. the center, whether literal, figurative or adverbial (especially with preposition)
H376: a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation)
H3820: the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything
H1961: to exist, i.e. be or become, come to pass (always emphatic, and not a mere copula or auxiliary)
H4347: a wound; figuratively, carnage, also pestilence
H3782: to totter or waver (through weakness of the legs, especially the ankle); by implication, to falter, stumble, faint or fall
H5921: above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
H5074: properly, to wave to and fro (rarely to flap up and down); figuratively, to rove, flee, or (causatively) to drive away
H3605: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
H120: ruddy i.e. a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.)
H5046: properly, to front, i.e. stand boldly out opposite; by implication (causatively), to manifest; figuratively, to announce (always by word of mouth to one present); specifically, to expose, predict, explain, praise
H4639: an action (good or bad); generally, a transaction; abstractly, activity; by implication, a product (specifically, a poem) or (generally) property
H7919: to be (causatively, make or act) circumspect and hence, intelligent
H8055: probably to brighten up, i.e. (figuratively) be (causatively, make) blithe or gleesome
H3068: Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
H2620: to flee for protection; figuratively, to confide in
H1984: to be clear (orig. of sound, but usually of color); to shine; hence, to make ashow, to boast; and thus to be (clamorously) foolish; to rave; causatively, to celebrate; also to stultify
